text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty SEV2 page triggered — elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for requests hitting us-west-2 ingress. Alert: 120m elevated 5xx rate, spike in 504 gateway timeouts. Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted).

Maya (on-call): I'm on it. Seeing 502/504s from the us-west API gateway, latency for a lot of requests around 5-8s then timeout. Starting investigation.

Maya (on-call): quick health checks: gateway frontends show CPU ok, but the gateway-worker pods have high retry loops and long tail latencies. Backend pool behind gateway shows large queue depth for kv-cache writes.

Lee (SRE): I'm seeing Redis replication lag on us-west primary -> replica (rdb-repl lag ~ 15s) and a backlog on the write queue. Metrics: redis-0 rdb_io_delay spiked, netty GC low but conn backlog high.

Daniel: Is this consistent with a KV replication stall? If the write path is blocked, requests that touch prefix cache may block and cause gateway retries -> 5xx. Any signs of disk pressure on redis nodes?

Maya (on-call): disk i/o for redis nodes is normal. Network retransmits spiking between redis-0 and redis-1 in us-west. Could be noisy NIC or kernel queue.

Alex (eng-runtime): We added a minor change yesterday to the async cache write path that increases in-flight buffers for high concurrency; could exacerbate replication. I'm rolling back that config on the canary pool now.

Maya (on-call): Ok coordinating rollback. Rolling restart of canary gateway-worker (us-west) to drain and pick up new config. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway-worker -n prod-us-west --selector=pool=canary`

support-bot: Customer impact: 27 customers reported elevated errors in the last 30m (support-triage). Top impacted account: acme-marketing-prod, calls to /v1/generate failing with 502.

Priya (support): I'll open a blocker status to Acme with the preliminary detail and ETA. Can you confirm mitigation steps so I can share?

Lee (SRE): Two parallel mitigations: 1) failover routing for new requests away from us-west to eu-west-1 for customers with geo-fallback enabled; 2) reduce KV write pressure by temporarily turning off synchronous replication for prefix caching (set cache.async_writes=true).

Daniel: Initiating request routing change for non-binding traffic. Running policy update: `redwood-router update-policy --from-region us-west-2 --to-region eu-west-1 --routes /v1/generate --condition best-effort`

Maya (on-call): Pushed policy. Observability: new request rates to eu-west-1 increase, 5xx rate in us-west starts to decline slowly. Still see retries for in-flight sessions that maintain us-west sticky routing.

Alex (eng-runtime): I just flipped cache.async_writes=true on the us-west cache tier and restarted the cache-workers. This should drop replication pressure. Watch redis replication lag.

Lee (SRE): Replication lag dropping from 15s -> 2s within 90s. Gateway retry loops decreasing. 5xx rate down 70% vs peak.

Maya (on-call): Good. Starting graceful failover for remaining sticky sessions: `redwood-session migrate --region us-west-2 --target eu-west-1 --grace-period 30s` — this will move new sessions over without hard-killing user flows.

support-bot: Support update queued to customers: short blip causing 5xx/timeout for some requests in us-west-2, mitigation in progress, ETA provisional 30-60m.

Priya (support): Notifying enterprise customers (pager) with link to status page: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/1775724001 — include note about cross-region failover and potential increased latency for EU-routed traffic.

Maya (on-call): Traffic now mostly served from eu-west. We see healthy p50/p95 latency from failover region, error rates stable. Scaling us-west cache-workers to 4 to help backlog drain.

Daniel: Observed root-cause hypothesis: kernel-level NIC flapping on one NIC in the us-west redis host plus increased in-flight buffer config amplified write backlog; combination caused replication stall and cascading gateway retries. Alex's config rollback plus async writes mitigated.

Lee (SRE): Continuing monitoring for 2 hours. I'll keep CPU/net/disk/redis-repl panels on. Creating a pinned dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/alerts/1775724001

Maya (on-call): Handoff: I'm taking a 30m break; handing to Daniel for active monitoring and SRE cleanup.

Daniel: Acknowledge takeover. I'll keep the page and coordinate with infra to inspect the NICs and schedule a host replacement if we see more flaps.

Priya (support): All external customers notified. Will send a follow-up once we have postmortem details and timeline.

Maya (on-call): Post-incident action items (quick): 1) revert in-flight buffer default (Alex to PR), 2) add auto-detect threshold for redis-repl-lag to trigger proactive routing, 3) infra to investigate NIC on redis-0 and replace if necessary.

Daniel: I'll own item 2 (routing automation) and coordinate with infra for item 3. Alex will own config PR. Maya will draft the incident summary for leadership.

Maya (on-call): Marking incident in slack as mitigated. Monitoring for 2h and will update status page with full postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 1775724001 status changed to MITIGATED by Maya. Duration: ~13 minutes to major mitigation, ongoing monitoring.

Daniel: Leaving final note: customers that saw errors may have partial requests retried; recommend informing product teams and checking async job replays for any duplicated submissions.

Priya (support): Noted. Will add duplication guidance to the customer follow-up.

Maya (on-call): Thanks team. Closing thread for active coordination, will reopen if we see regression.
